findings.title: US equity allocation exceeds target drift tolerance
findings.detail: The portfolio is overweight in US equities by {{m:drift.US_EQUITY.pp}} percentage points, exceeding the tolerance of {{m:cfg.drift_tolerance.pp}}. This is likely contributing to the drift away from the balanced model. Rebalancing is recommended to align with the target allocation of {{m:target.US_EQUITY.pct}}.

findings.title: Canadian bond allocation below target drift tolerance
findings.detail: The portfolio is underweight in Canadian bonds by {{m:drift.CA_BONDS.pp}} percentage points, exceeding the tolerance of {{m:cfg.drift_tolerance.pp}}. This significant deviation from the target of {{m:target.CA_BONDS.pct}} warrants attention to restore the balanced risk profile.

Cash in the non-registered account is at {{m:alloc.CASH.pct}}, which is above the target of {{m:target.CASH.pct}}. This aligns with the note regarding the uninvested bonus. Deploying this cash into the underweight asset classes could help reduce overall portfolio drift.
findings.title: Excess cash in non-registered account contributing to drift
US-listed fund held in TFSA
findings.detail: The US-listed fund USEQ is held in the TFSA. Under educational tax-location principles, US-listed securities in a TFSA may be subject to foreign withholding tax on dividends that cannot be recovered. Consider relocating this to a non-registered account or RRSP if appropriate for the client's long-term strategy.

The client has {{m:tax.tfsa_room.cad}} of unused TFSA room, while {{m:tax.nonreg_interest.cad}} in interest-generating assets is held in a non-registered account. Moving interest-bearing assets to a tax-sheltered account can improve tax efficiency by sheltering interest income from personal income tax.
findings.title: Unused TFSA room with interest-bearing assets in non-registered account
Interest-income holdings in non-registered account
findings.detail: The client holds {{m:tax.nonreg_interest.cad}} in interest-generating assets within a non-registered account. Interest income is typically taxed at the client's full marginal tax rate. Educational tax-location rules suggest prioritizing tax-advantaged accounts for these assets to optimize after-tax returns.

US equity markets experienced significant growth, with the index returning {{m:mkt.us_equity_ytd.pct}} percent year to date. This performance, driven by technology sector gains, likely caused an overweight drift in the US equity portion of the portfolio.
findings.title: US equity growth contributed to portfolio drift
Canadian equity and energy sector volatility influenced allocation
findings.detail: Canadian equity performance was more moderate at {{m:mkt.ca_equity_ytd.pct}} percent year to date. Additionally, the energy sector faced volatility, declining {{m:mkt.energy_sector_qtd.pct}} percent quarter to date, which impacted the broader Canadian equity allocation.

findings.title: Lower Canadian bond yields affected fixed income holdings
findings.detail: Canadian bond yields have trended lower, with the ten-year yield currently at {{m:mkt.ca_10y_yield.pct}} percent. The bond index returned {{m:mkt.ca_bond_ytd.pct}} percent year to date, reflecting the cooling inflation environment and impacting the fixed income component of the portfolio.

findings.title: International equity and real asset performance contributed to drift
findings.detail: International equities returned {{m:mkt.intl_equity_ytd.pct}} percent year to date, while real assets, represented by the REIT index, returned {{m:mkt.reit_ytd.pct}} percent. These returns contributed to the overall drift in the non-domestic and real asset segments of the client portfolio.

The portfolio volatility of {{m:risk.vol.pct}} is within the {{m:risk.vol_band_max.pct}} limit for a balanced profile. The portfolio is well-aligned with the model volatility of {{m:risk.target_vol.pct}}.
findings.title: Portfolio volatility is within suitability limits

findings.detail: A simulated equity bear market scenario results in a loss of {{m:stress.equity_bear.cad}}, representing a {{m:stress.equity_bear.pct}} decline in total portfolio value. Given the client's twenty-year horizon, this downside is manageable.
findings.title: Portfolio downside in equity bear scenario

findings.detail: No single security exceeds the concentration limit of {{m:conc.limit.pct}}. The portfolio maintains appropriate diversification across asset classes.
findings.title: No single-security concentration issues detected
